question_text: What would be the shape of the demand curve so that the total revenue curve is (a) a positively sloped straight line passing through the origin? (b) a horizontal line?

mcq_options.option_text: a positively sloped straight line passing through the origin?

question_image.description: Diagram illustrating the relationship between demand curve and total revenue curve.

parts.part_text: If the total revenue curve is a positively sloped straight line passing through the origin, then the slope of the demand curve will be a horizontal line parallel to the x-axis.
parts.answer_text: The demand curve will be horizontal.
parts.final_answer: Therefore, the demand curve is horizontal.

parts.part_text: If the total revenue curve is a horizontal line, then the demand curve will be downward sloping.
parts.answer_text: The demand curve will be downward sloping.
parts.final_answer: Thus, the demand curve is downward sloping.

difficulty_reasoning: Requires understanding of the relationship between demand and total revenue curves.

subject: economics
question_text: What is the value of the MR when the demand curve is elastic?
answer_text: When the demand curve is elastic (e > 1), then according to the relationship MR = P(1 - 1/e), the marginal revenue will be positive when price is positive.
final_answer: Thus, MR will be positive when P is positive.
difficulty_reasoning: Requires understanding of the relationship between price elasticity and marginal revenue.

subject: economics
question_text: Will the monopolist firm continue to produce in the short run if a loss is incurred at the best short run level of output?
answer_text: A monopolist firm can earn losses in the short run if the price is less than the minimum of AC. But if the price falls below the minimum of AVC, then the monopolist will stop production. The firm will continue to produce when the price is in between the minimum of AVC and the minimum of AC.
final_answer: Thus, the monopolist will continue production as long as the price is above AVC but below AC.
difficulty_reasoning: Requires understanding of cost structures in monopolistic markets.

subject: economics
question_text: Explain why the demand curve facing a firm under monopolistic competition is negatively sloped.
answer_text: A monopolistic firm has differentiated products; thus, it has to lower its price in order to increase its sales. Further, the products of different monopolistic firms are close substitutes to each other. Hence, the demand for all the products is elastic. For this reason, the demand curve is negatively sloped.
final_answer: Therefore, the demand curve is negatively sloped due to product differentiation and elasticity.
difficulty_reasoning: Involves understanding of market structures and demand elasticity.

subject: economics
question_text: What is the reason for the long run equilibrium of a firm in monopolistic competition to be associated with zero profit?
answer_text: The long run time horizon is featured by the free entry and exit of firms. If the firms in the short run are earning abnormal or super normal profits, then, new firms will be attracted to enter the market. Due to the new entrants, the market supply will increase. It leads to the reduction in the price that ultimately falls sufficiently to become equal to the minimum of average cost. When the market price is equal to the minimum of AC, it implies that all the firms earn normal profit or zero economic profit. On the contrary, if in the short run the firms are earning abnormal losses, then the existing firms will stop production and exit the market. This will lead to a decrease in the market supply, which will ultimately raise the price. The price will continue to rise until it becomes equal to the minimum of AC. 'Price = AC' implies that in the long run all the firms will earn zero economic profit. Hence, when the price is equal to the minimum of AC, neither any existing firm will exit nor any new firm will enter the market.
final_answer: Thus, in the long run, firms in monopolistic competition earn zero economic profit due to free market entry and exit.
difficulty_reasoning: Involves understanding of market dynamics and equilibrium concepts.

subject: economics
question_text: What is meant by prices being rigid? How can oligopoly behaviour lead to such an outcome?
answer_text: Price rigidity implies that the price is unresponsive to the changes in demand. This is because of the fact that even if any firm raises the price of its product with the motive of earning higher profits, the other firm will not do so, and the first firm will lose its customers. On the other hand, if one firm lowers its price in order to earn higher profits by maximising its sales, then in response, the other firm may also reduce the price. Consequently, the increase in total market sales is shared by both the firms. The firm that initiated selling at a lower price may get a lower share of the increase than expected. Therefore, the firms do not change their prices due to the fear of rival's reaction. Hence, there is no incentive for any firm to change its price. That is why the prices are regarded as rigid prices or sticky prices.
final_answer: Thus, prices are regarded as rigid or sticky due to the fear of competitive reactions among firms in an oligopoly.

subject: economics
question_text: If duopoly behaviour is one that is described by Cournot, the market demand curve is given by the equation q = 200 - 4p and both the firms have zero costs, find the quantity supplied by each firm in equilibrium and the equilibrium market price.
answer_text: When the demand curve is a straight line and total cost is zero, the duopolist finds it most profitable to supply half of the maximum demand of a good. At P = Rs 0, market demand is Q = 200 - 4(0) = 200 units. If firm B does not produce anything, then the market demand faced by firm A is 200 units. Thus, the supply of firm A = 100 units. In the next round, the portion of market demand faced by firm B is 100 units. Thus, firm B would supply = 50 units. Therefore, the equilibrium market price can be calculated as follows: P = 50.

steps.description: Calculate total market demand at price zero.
Determine supply of firm A when firm B produces nothing.
Determine supply of firm B based on firm A's supply.

final_answer: Thus, the equilibrium market price is Rs 50.
difficulty_reasoning: Involves calculations based on demand and supply principles.
